title: I built a free browser game where you chair the World AI Council — or play as the superintelligence. Notes on splitting Claude and Grok.
author: albertsimondev
selftext:
Built **AIRIS** as a free browser strategy game about trusting a rising superintelligence from 2026 to 2076.

You either:

* chair the World AI Council (approve/refuse requests, audits, crises, votes), or
* play as AIRIS itself with a secret goal and try not to get shut down.

\~25 min per run, 37 endings, plus a Daily scenario. No sign-up; progress saves in the browser. Desktop + mobile.

**Play:** [vaigames.com/airis](https://vaigames.com/airis/)  
**Trailer:** [youtu.be](https://youtu.be/Y-qRw1Svzvc)

# How I split the AI tools

* **Claude** for most of the game systems, council/AI logic, and long-form writing.
* **Grok** for brainstorming endings, crisis beats, and quick iteration when I was stuck.
* Art / music / graphics also AI-assisted; I directed and edited everything into one loop.

Happy to answer process questions (prompting the two sides without them collapsing into the same game, Daily generation, ending coverage). Feedback on pacing and whether the AI side feels fair is especially useful.
